messages:
maria: quick heads-up — opened a docs PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/432. The Dedicated autoscale section mixes up preemption vs eviction and the SLA language feels misleading to customers. Can someone help reword and add a concise SDK example for the scale policy?

devon: @maria looking now. TL;DR: for Dedicated we should avoid saying "preemptible" unless talking about burst/spot pools. For reserved Dedicated, call it 'reservation eviction' when we reclaim capacity for billing/account reasons.

kevin: agree. User-facing text should use 'eviction' for any forced termination, and 'fallback routing' for automatic model routing to backups. Propose this sentence: "Dedicated workloads may be subject to eviction in rare capacity reclamation events; Reserved Commit tiers have stronger protection — see SLA matrix." Keep it short. :thinking_face:

sre-jen: also add a small section clarifying isolation modes — customers can choose soft-affinity (best-effort co-location with isolation controls) vs hard-affinity (tenant-pinned hosts). Hard-affinity == lower eviction risk but higher cost. Include expected MTTR for evictions (~5-20 min depending on region) and a note about automatic fallback policies.

maria: putting a compact SDK snippet here to propose for the PR. If this looks ok I'll paste into the migration guide under "Autoscale policy examples (Dedicated)":

```python
# Dedicated autoscale policy example (Python SDK pseudocode)
policy = {
    "min_replicas": 2,
    "max_replicas": 20,
    "scale_step": 2,
    "cpu_target_pct": 65,
    "cooldown_seconds": 300,
    "isolation": "hard",  # options: soft | hard
    "eviction_protection": "reserved_commit",  # not supported for burst pools
}
client.create_dedicated_pool(name="prod-llm", policy=policy)
```

devon: snippet looks good, two small notes: rename `eviction_protection` -> `reservation_protection` (more precise), and change `cpu_target_pct` -> `util_target_pct` since we also autoscale by token throughput in runtime. Also we should add a one-liner example in Terraform later.

maria: thanks. I'll update the snippet. Also found that the SLA matrix anchor link in the PR points to #dedicated-sla but the docs site uses #sla-dedicated — docs-bot flagged it.

docs-bot: Link checker: https://docs.redwood.ai/dedicated#dedicated-sla -> 404 (anchor mismatch). Please update to https://docs.redwood.ai/dedicated#sla-dedicated.

lia: I'll fix the anchor and add the isolation paragraph and the updated SDK snippet to the PR. I'll also add a short footnote clarifying "reservation protection only applies to Reserved Commit tiers".

kevin: thanks @lia — can you also add a short user-facing example describing fallback routing behavior? one sentence + pointer to routing docs should be enough.

lia: yep. I'll push a small commit and tag @devon for sign-off. Targeting this afternoon. :shipit:

maria: perfect — assign PR to lia, devon for review, and kevin for the wording check. Thanks all!
